note.question: When should a supplier or other privately informed negotiator disclose information, and how does the answer change when disclosure can affect not only bargaining but also which partner will negotiate with it?
note.overview: Privately informed bargainers strategically choose whether to make a credible costly disclosure, and, when disclosure precedes matching, that action changes beliefs and partner assignment before bargaining. The paper derives incentive-compatible bargaining benchmarks and pure-strategy disclosure equilibria, then tests them in controlled human-subject experiments.

components.label: Incentive-compatible bargaining focal equilibria with disclosure and matching equilibria
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Incentive-compatible bargaining focal equilibria with disclosure and matching equilibria. The efficient focal equilibrium has certain agreement and gives the informed high type an information rent; the equal-split focal equilibrium requires γ_h=1 and γ_l=[(1/2)π_h]/[π_h-(1/2)π_l]. After random matching, Result 1 implies that only the low type may strictly disclose, and only in the equal-split case at sufficiently low d. Before endogenous matching, four pure disclosure profiles can arise, and Result 2 identifies a nondegenerate parameter set for which only the informed high type discloses in the unique pure disclosure equilibrium under either bargaining focal point.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In the random-matching setting, an informed and an uninformed player are matched, the informed player learns type and may credibly disclose it at cost d, and the pair bargains. In the endogenous-matching setting, two informed players learn their types and simultaneously decide whether to disclose; uninformed players observe disclosure, the more attractive uninformed player receives matching priority, and each resulting pair bargains separately. After random matching, disclosure can restore complete information and reduce inefficient disagreement but sacrifices any information rent and costs d. Before matching, disclosure additionally changes the probability of receiving the more attractive partner.
